Ruckus purchase price allocation is preliminary and in-process R&D has no fair value yet (10-Q Q3 page:12); Ruckus contributes from July 1, 2026 only, so no standalone Ruckus history or LTM pro forma EBITDA is supplied. A pro forma revenue, net income and EPS table exists (10-Q Q3 page:13) but no pro forma EBITDA.
No discrete fourth quarter FY2025 or LTM figures are printed. FY2025 is annual only.
Ratings, market quotes, peer set, valuation inputs, sponsor and legal documents are blank in the context.
Extraction fidelity not reviewed: each source is a text extraction; table layout and any images or charts were not inspected. Source quality and extraction status are distinct.
Management claims in the releases (for example record results, data center agreement, Q4 2026 guidance) are attributed management language, not filed fact.
Entity and instrument roles located — paragraph 1

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Belden is a profitable, cash-generative manufacturer whose capital structure was transformed on July 1, 2026. Before the Ruckus acquisition, debt was three euro senior subordinated notes totalling USD 1,292.0 million at FY2025 against Adjusted EBITDA of USD 458.7 million, and a revolver that had been drawn and repaid within 2025. At September 27, 2026, debt is USD 3,103.8 million before unamortised costs: USD 1,253.8 million of euro notes (2028, 2031 and the new 2033 series) and USD 1,850.0 million of Term Loan B due 2033, which the company priced at term SOFR plus 2.25%. Cash is USD 380.7 million and the USD 400.0 million revolver is undrawn, with USD 373.5 million available. On trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 557.2 million, which includes Ruckus for one quarter only, total debt is 5.57x and net debt 4.89x. Those ratios are conservative against a full-year combined base but cannot be restated, because Ruckus earnings before July 1, 2026 are not supplied. GAAP results for Q3 2026 were a net loss of USD 11.4 million because of USD 100 million of purchase-accounting charges that the company excludes from Adjusted EBITDA; the Ruckus loss before tax in the quarter was USD 63.1 million. The company's earlier long-term net leverage goal of about 1.5x appears in the 10-K and the Q1 2026 10-Q, and is absent from the Q2 and Q3 2026 10-Qs. Net interest expense was USD 41.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 11.6 million in Q3 2025, and nine months 2026 operating cash flow less capital expenditure and disposal proceeds (the company's free cash flow) was USD 107.4 million against USD 97.6 million. The term loan amortises USD 18.5 million a year (0.25% a quarter of USD 1,850.0 million). Legal terms of the new term loan (covenants, security, guarantors) are not in the supplied sources.

facts.text: Adjusted EBITDA is the company's non-GAAP measure, built from net income plus depreciation, amortisation of intangibles and of software development intangibles, tax, net interest, restructuring and integration costs, debt extinguishment and acquisition adjustments (10-Q Q3 page 32). For nine months 2026 it adds back USD 59.4 million (59,363 thousand) of acquisition and divestiture adjustments, primarily the fair value step-up of acquired inventory, and USD 36,696 thousand of severance, restructuring and integration costs. The MD&A attributes part of the increase in gross profit and Adjusted EBITDA to tariff refunds: USD 17.9 million on 2025 transactions in nine months 2026 (USD 4.3 million in Q3), plus USD 8.1 million net on 2026 transactions that offsets 2026 tariff cost (10-Q Q3 pages 25 and 28). Analyst interpretation: refunds of past-year tariffs are unlikely to recur at that level, and they are inside Adjusted EBITDA. No covenant EBITDA definition is supplied, so the company measure should not be read as covenant EBITDA.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. LTM Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026 = FY2025 458,734 + nine months 2026 435,104 - nine months 2025 336,672 = 557,166. Inputs: 10-K page 41; 10-Q Q3 page 32. 2. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Belden is a US-listed manufacturer of copper and fiber cable, connectivity, industrial networking and security products sold mainly through distributors, which moved in 2026 from a low-leverage, buyback-oriented company to one carrying USD 3,103.8 million of debt after a debt-funded acquisition. The Ruckus purchase (wireless access points, switches, cloud management and software, bought from Vistance Networks) closed July 1, 2026 for USD 1,869.6 million net of cash acquired, funded by a USD 1,850.0 million seven-year Term Loan B. For creditors the mechanics are: Ruckus is consolidated for one quarter only, so trailing leverage of 5.57x is on a partial earnings base; the purchase price allocation is preliminary; and goodwill and intangibles of USD 2,040.8 million (the sum of the two printed allocation lines) now sit against equity of USD 1,392.0 million. Management describes record demand in 2026, but that is attributed management language. Belden is NYSE-listed and no sponsor or controlling holder appears in the supplied sources, so sponsor-extraction behaviour is not documented, and neither is any sponsor equity support. What is missing is as important as what is present: the Term Loan B, revolver and indenture documents are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions, additional debt and collateral release cannot be judged. Governance conclusions here are limited to documented issuer actions.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Ruckus. On April 29, 2026 Belden signed a definitive agreement to acquire certain entities comprising Ruckus Networks, for approximately USD 1.846 billion to be funded through additional debt (10-Q Q1 pages 16 and 19); the April 30, 2026 release names the seller as Vistance Networks (Nasdaq: VISN) and gives approximately USD 1.85 billion (release page 1). The acquisition closed July 1, 2026 for USD 1,869.6 million net of cash acquired and is accounted for as a business combination (10-Q Q3 page 11). The three descriptions of price differ in rounding and basis (signed price, rounded price, closing price net of cash); the closing figure in the 10-Q controls. The preliminary allocation records receivables USD 146.457 million, inventory USD 153.555 million, intangible assets USD 1,040.0 million (developed technologies USD 800.0 million over 5.0 years, customer relationships USD 160.0 million over 15.0 years, trademarks USD 80.0 million over 20.0 years), goodwill USD 1,000.819 million, and liabilities assumed USD 535.212 million including deferred income taxes USD 175.882 million (10-Q Q3 pages 11-12). In-process R&D has no fair value yet and the allocation may change (page 12). Ruckus contributed USD 167.8 million of revenue and a USD 63.1 million loss before taxes in Q3 2026, after USD 56.3 million of inventory fair value charges and USD 43.7 million of intangible amortisation (page 13). Pro forma revenue and net income as if acquired on January 1, 2025 are printed, but not EBITDA (page 13). Status: completed; integration is management's stated focus (release October 29, 2026, page 2, Management Language).

facts.text: New debt and use of proceeds. (1) Term Loan B: USD 1,850.0 million, entered July 1, 2026 to fund Ruckus, term SOFR plus 2.25% or base rate plus 1.25%, amortising 0.25% a quarter, maturing July 1, 2033, issued at a discount of USD 4.6 million with USD 38.8 million of fees; fair value approximates carrying value (10-Q Q3 page 20). Guarantors, security and covenants are not described. (2) EUR 450.0 million 4.250% senior subordinated notes due 2033, issued January 28, 2026 (10-K page 107, Note 25), guaranteed on a senior subordinated basis by current and future domestic subsidiaries, ranking equal to the 2028 and 2031 notes, with fees of USD 8.6 million (10-Q Q3 page 20); proceeds with cash on hand funded the full repurchase of the EUR 450.0 million 3.375% notes due 2027 on February 11, 2026 for USD 535.9 million, with a USD 1.3 million loss on extinguishment (10-Q Q3 page 18; the 10-K quotes USD 537.3 million, a translation difference carried from the readiness review). (3) Revolver: a USD 50.0 million draw on June 29, 2026 was repaid in full on September 25, 2026 (page 18). Liquidity effect: per the financial base, liquidity at September 27, 2026 is USD 754.2 million (cash USD 380.7 million plus revolver availability USD 373.5 million). Refinancing effect: the 2027 maturity was removed; the next fixed maturities are the 2028 notes and the Term Loan B amortisation of USD 18.5 million a year. Sponsor: none. Ratings agencies' reactions: Not supplied.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Evidence: Ruckus contributed USD 167.8 million of revenue and a USD 63.1 million loss before taxes in Q3 2026 and is funded by a USD 1,850.0 million term loan (10-Q Q3 pages 13 and 20). Mechanic: the earnings that service the new debt are unproven and include non-cash charges that will fade, while cash interest begins in full. Implication: debt service and leverage tolerance depend on Ruckus delivering earnings; the 5.57x trailing ratio (CP-1) is on a partial base and is not a stable measure. Countering item: none logged except the price-basis discrepancy. 2. Evidence: ten largest customers are about 47% of revenue, eight of them distributors, with no minimum purchase obligations (10-K pages 5-6 and 106). Mechanic: channel destocking or a distributor change moves volume quickly, and short backlog limits visibility. Implication: revenue durability depends on distributor behaviour; backlog was USD 567.7 million at December 31, 2025 with almost all shipping in 2026. 3. Evidence: copper pricing is passed through with a lag (10-K pages 9-10) and tariff refunds of USD 17.9 million were recorded (10-Q Q3 page 25). Mechanic: margins have a timing exposure to copper and tariff policy; refunds boost reported results without recurring. Implication: margin resilience should be judged excluding the refunds on 2025 transactions; the amounts are disclosed for Q3 2026 and nine months 2026, while the refunds on 2026 transactions net to zero against tariff cost (10-Q Q3 page 25). 4. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder appears in the supplied sources. Mechanic: no sponsor extraction behaviour is documented, but there is also no sponsor equity support. Implication: sponsor alignment is Insufficient Information rather than adverse.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: 1. Goodwill plus amortisable intangibles acquired: 1,000,819 + 1,040,000 = 2,040,819 (USD thousands), equal to the printed total of USD 2,040.819 million (10-Q Q3 page 12); the allocation total of assets acquired is 2,404,844 and liabilities 535,212, giving net assets of 1,869,632, consistent with the 1,869.6 million consideration (page 11). 2. Geography, nine months 2026: 1,604,739 + 485,850 + 321,897 = 2,412,486, equal to total revenues. 3. facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Belden is a cash-generative manufacturer whose credit profile weakened in 2026 because it borrowed to buy Ruckus, so the credit now turns on whether Ruckus earns what the debt needs. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 754.2 million, an undrawn revolver due in 2030 and no maturity of the euro notes before 2028. The weakest point is leverage: total debt of USD 3,103.8 million is 5.57x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, which holds Ruckus for one quarter only, against 2.82x at FY2025. What decides the outcome is Ruckus earnings after a USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026, and the unsupplied term loan terms. Category: Analyst Interpretation, built on the cited financial base and business context.

The strongest support is liquidity of USD 754.2 million, an undrawn revolver due in 2030 and no maturity of the euro notes before 2028. The weakest point is leverage: total debt of USD 3,103.8 million is 5.57x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, which holds Ruckus for one quarter only, against 2.82x at FY2025. What decides the outcome is Ruckus earnings after a USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026, and the unsupplied term loan terms. Category: Analyst Interpretation, built on the cited financial base and business context.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the capital structure changed in July 2026. Belden's debt rose from USD 1,291.950 million at FY2025 to USD 3,103.780 million at Q3 2026 before unamortised costs, because a USD 1,850.0 million Term Loan B funded Ruckus (Documentary Fact; financial base debt register and business context transaction summary). The mechanic is that the debt is carried in full while Ruckus earnings are in the trailing base for one quarter only; the implication is that the 5.57x total and 4.89x net leverage ratios are upper bounds on the true level, but the true level cannot be calculated because Ruckus pre-acquisition earnings are not supplied (Analyst Interpretation).

The only near-term scheduled debt payment is Term Loan B amortisation of USD 18.5 million a year; the first euro note maturity is the 2028 series (Documentary Fact). 1. LTM Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026 = FY2025 458,734 + nine months 2026 435,104 - nine months 2025 336,672 = 557,166. Inputs: 10-K page 41; 10-Q Q3 page 32.

2. Total debt, Q3 2026 = notes 1,253,780 + Term Loan B 1,850,000 = 3,103,780; this equals the USD 3,103.8 million carrying value stated on 10-Q Q3 page 20. Less unamortised costs 53,370 gives 3,050,410, which equals the balance sheet (18,500 + 3,031,910).
6. EBITDA / cash interest, FY2025 = 458,734 / 43,157 = 10.63x. Q3 2026: Not calculable, cash interest paid not printed.

8. Liquidity, Q3 2026 = cash 380,706 + revolver availability 373,500 = 754,206 (USD 754.2 million). FY2025 = 389,887 + 383,900 = 773,787. Net of letters of credit by facility: Not calculable, because the filings print the letters of credit as a total without saying how much is issued under the Revolver. The commitment less availability is 400,000 - 373,500 = 26,500 at Q3 2026; the sources do not attribute that gap.

9. Free cash flow, FY2025 (company definition: operating cash flow less capital expenditures plus disposal proceeds) = 354,864 - 136,172 + 191 = 218,883. Nine months 2026 as printed 107,444 = 240,200 - 132,863 + 107.

10. Funding cross-check: borrowings under credit arrangements 2,432,630 compare with Term Loan B 1,850,000 + 2033 Notes 537,300 at issuance + revolver draw 50,000 - discount 4,600 = 2,432,700 (difference 70, rounding of the stated USD 537.3 million and USD 4.6 million). Payments under borrowing arrangements 585,860 compare with 2027 Notes repurchase 535,900 + revolver repayment 50,000 = 585,900 (difference 40, rounding).
11. Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation re-added from the printed rows: FY2025 458,734, nine months 2026 435,104, nine months 2025 336,672 and Q3 2026 171,137 each equal the printed totals.

12. Nominal growth, Q3 2026 revenue over Q3 2025: 965,954 / 698,221 - 1 = 38.3%, which agrees with the 38% in the release; the release attributes 11% to organic growth, 24% to acquisitions and 3% to copper pass-through (release page 6).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Belden is a US-listed network-infrastructure manufacturer that bought Ruckus on July 1, 2026 with a USD 1,850.0 million term loan, adding wireless and software revenue but also debt, integration and purchase-accounting risk. | Medium | The term loan agreement, ownership data and Ruckus history are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Ruckus added USD 167.8 million of revenue and a USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026, and the purchase accounting is preliminary. | Earnings contribution is unproven, and the new term loan carries the acquisition risk. | High |

| Revenue runs through distributors: the ten largest customers are about 47% of FY2025 revenue and the largest distributor about 14%. | Concentration and a lack of purchase commitments make volumes depend on channel behaviour. | High |

| Share repurchases were USD 195.6 million in FY2025 and USD 31.8 million in nine months 2026, and the net leverage goal is absent from the Q2 and Q3 2026 filings. | Capital return fell when debt rose; whether it resumes ahead of deleveraging is undocumented. | Medium |

| Deferred revenue rose to USD 250.6 million from USD 49.7 million at the start of 2026, mostly acquired. | Support and software revenue is added to a mostly point-in-time hardware model, with limited history to judge. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

Belden is a US-listed manufacturer of copper and fiber cable, connectivity, industrial networking and security products sold mainly through distributors, which moved in 2026 from a low-leverage, buyback-oriented company to one carrying USD 3,103.8 million of debt after a debt-funded acquisition. The Ruckus purchase (wireless access points, switches, cloud management and software, bought from Vistance Networks) closed July 1, 2026 for USD 1,869.6 million net of cash acquired, funded by a USD 1,850.0 million seven-year Term Loan B. For creditors the mechanics are: Ruckus is consolidated for one quarter only, so trailing leverage of 5.57x is on a partial earnings base; the purchase price allocation is preliminary; and goodwill and intangibles of USD 2,040.8 million (the sum of the two printed allocation lines) now sit against equity of USD 1,392.0 million. Management describes record demand in 2026, but that is attributed management language. Belden is NYSE-listed and no sponsor or controlling holder appears in the supplied sources, so sponsor-extraction behaviour is not documented, and neither is any sponsor equity support. What is missing is as important as what is present: the Term Loan B, revolver and indenture documents are not in the pack, so legal capacity for distributions, additional debt and collateral release cannot be judged. Governance conclusions here are limited to documented issuer actions.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Ruckus. On April 29, 2026 Belden signed a definitive agreement to acquire certain entities comprising Ruckus Networks, for approximately USD 1.846 billion to be funded through additional debt (10-Q Q1 pages 16 and 19); the April 30, 2026 release names the seller as Vistance Networks (Nasdaq: VISN) and gives approximately USD 1.85 billion (release page 1). The acquisition closed July 1, 2026 for USD 1,869.6 million net of cash acquired and is accounted for as a business combination (10-Q Q3 page 11). The three descriptions of price differ in rounding and basis (signed price, rounded price, closing price net of cash); the closing figure in the 10-Q controls. The preliminary allocation records receivables USD 146.457 million, inventory USD 153.555 million, intangible assets USD 1,040.0 million (developed technologies USD 800.0 million over 5.0 years, customer relationships USD 160.0 million over 15.0 years, trademarks USD 80.0 million over 20.0 years), goodwill USD 1,000.819 million, and liabilities assumed USD 535.212 million including deferred income taxes USD 175.882 million (10-Q Q3 pages 11-12). In-process R&D has no fair value yet and the allocation may change (page 12). Ruckus contributed USD 167.8 million of revenue and a USD 63.1 million loss before taxes in Q3 2026, after USD 56.3 million of inventory fair value charges and USD 43.7 million of intangible amortisation (page 13). Pro forma revenue and net income as if acquired on January 1, 2025 are printed, but not EBITDA (page 13). Status: completed; integration is management's stated focus (release October 29, 2026, page 2, Management Language).

New debt and use of proceeds. (1) Term Loan B: USD 1,850.0 million, entered July 1, 2026 to fund Ruckus, term SOFR plus 2.25% or base rate plus 1.25%, amortising 0.25% a quarter, maturing July 1, 2033, issued at a discount of USD 4.6 million with USD 38.8 million of fees; fair value approximates carrying value (10-Q Q3 page 20). Guarantors, security and covenants are not described. (2) EUR 450.0 million 4.250% senior subordinated notes due 2033, issued January 28, 2026 (10-K page 107, Note 25), guaranteed on a senior subordinated basis by current and future domestic subsidiaries, ranking equal to the 2028 and 2031 notes, with fees of USD 8.6 million (10-Q Q3 page 20); proceeds with cash on hand funded the full repurchase of the EUR 450.0 million 3.375% notes due 2027 on February 11, 2026 for USD 535.9 million, with a USD 1.3 million loss on extinguishment (10-Q Q3 page 18; the 10-K quotes USD 537.3 million, a translation difference carried from the readiness review). (3) Revolver: a USD 50.0 million draw on June 29, 2026 was repaid in full on September 25, 2026 (page 18). Liquidity effect: per the financial base, liquidity at September 27, 2026 is USD 754.2 million (cash USD 380.7 million plus revolver availability USD 373.5 million). ## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Belden has strong liquidity but, after the debt-funded Ruckus purchase, much higher leverage that rests on unproven acquired earnings. The credit view is cautious and depends on Ruckus delivering. | Medium | Term loan terms, Ruckus earnings history and ratings are not supplied. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt is USD 3,103.8 million, 5.57x trailing Adjusted EBITDA against 2.82x at FY2025. | The ratio is overstated by one-quarter Ruckus earnings, but the true level cannot be measured without Ruckus history. | High |
| Liquidity is USD 754.2 million, with an undrawn revolver due in 2030. | Near-term liquidity risk is low; no bond falls due before 2028. | High |
| Ruckus lost USD 63.1 million before tax in Q3 2026 and its purchase accounting is preliminary. | Debt service depends on acquired earnings that are not yet proven. | High |
| Revenue depends on distributors: the ten largest customers are about 47% of FY2025 revenue. | Volumes can swing with channel behaviour; backlog gives limited visibility. | High |
### Credit view

Belden is a cash-generative manufacturer whose credit profile weakened in 2026 because it borrowed to buy Ruckus, so the credit now turns on whether Ruckus earns what the debt needs. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 754.2 million, an undrawn revolver due in 2030 and no maturity of the euro notes before 2028. The weakest point is leverage: total debt of USD 3,103.8 million is 5.57x trailing Adjusted EBITDA, which holds Ruckus for one quarter only, against 2.82x at FY2025. What decides the outcome is Ruckus earnings after a USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026, and the unsupplied term loan terms. Category: Analyst Interpretation, built on the cited financial base and business context.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Content | Category and basis | Confidence |

| Assessment | Cautious fundamental view: strong liquidity and solid legacy cash generation, offset by sharply higher debt, a partial-period earnings base and unproven acquired earnings | Analyst Interpretation; financial base (leverage, liquidity, free cash flow) and business context (Ruckus, concentration) | Medium |

| Thesis | Belden's liquidity and legacy cash generation support the new debt only if Ruckus earnings arrive, because leverage rose to 5.57x trailing Adjusted EBITDA on a partial earnings base | Analyst Interpretation; same basis | Medium |

Confidence is below High because the business context records unsupplied term loan documents, unsupplied Ruckus history and unsupplied ownership and ratings, and the financial base records the same limits.
### Key findings

First, the capital structure changed in July 2026. Belden's debt rose from USD 1,291.950 million at FY2025 to USD 3,103.780 million at Q3 2026 before unamortised costs, because a USD 1,850.0 million Term Loan B funded Ruckus (Documentary Fact; financial base debt register and business context transaction summary). The mechanic is that the debt is carried in full while Ruckus earnings are in the trailing base for one quarter only; the implication is that the 5.57x total and 4.89x net leverage ratios are upper bounds on the true level, but the true level cannot be calculated because Ruckus pre-acquisition earnings are not supplied (Analyst Interpretation).

Second, liquidity is sound. Cash is USD 380.7 million and revolver availability is USD 373.5 million, giving USD 754.2 million, with the USD 400.0 million revolver due in 2030 and undrawn at September 27, 2026 (Documentary Fact; financial base liquidity). The only near-term scheduled debt payment is Term Loan B amortisation of USD 18.5 million a year; the first euro note maturity is the 2028 series (Documentary Fact). A springing fixed charge test applies to the revolver only if borrowings exceed 90% of the combined borrowing base or availability falls below USD 27.0 million (Documentary Fact); the test level is not supplied.

Third, earnings quality needs care. Adjusted EBITDA is a company measure that for nine months 2026 adds back USD 59.4 million of acquisition adjustments and includes tariff refunds of USD 17.9 million on 2025 transactions (Documentary Fact). Refunds of past-year tariffs are unlikely to recur at that level, so reported margin of 18.0% for nine months 2026 overstates the underlying run rate by an amount that cannot be measured from the sources (Analyst Interpretation).

Fourth, cash flow is positive but the post-deal interest burden is not yet visible in it. Free cash flow was USD 107.4 million for nine months 2026 against USD 97.6 million a year earlier, but carries one quarter of Term Loan B interest. Net interest expense was USD 41.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 11.6 million in Q3 2025 (Documentary Fact). Cash interest for 2026 is not supplied, so interest cover on a cash basis is Not calculable; the net-expense cover of 6.85x on a trailing basis is a substitute that mixes one quarter of the new interest with a partial earnings base (Analyst Interpretation).

Fifth, the business depends on its distributors and on Ruckus integration. The largest distributor is about 14% of FY2025 revenue and the ten largest customers about 47%, with no minimum purchase commitments (Documentary Fact). Ruckus contributed USD 167.8 million of revenue and a USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026 after non-cash purchase-accounting charges, and the allocation of the USD 1,869.6 million net purchase price is preliminary (Documentary Fact). Management says demand is robust and has announced a USD 100 million data center supply agreement for 2027 (Management Language, not adopted).

Sixth, capital allocation tilted toward shareholders before the deal and is undocumented after it. Share repurchases were USD 195.6 million in FY2025 and USD 31.8 million in nine months 2026, and the long-term net leverage goal of about 1.5x no longer appears in the Q2 and Q3 2026 filings (Documentary Fact). No replacement leverage target or deleveraging path is documented; this is a gap, not an adverse conclusion (Insufficient Information).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) Liquidity of USD 754.2 million with an undrawn revolver due in 2030 and no euro note maturity before 2028 (Documentary Fact). (2) Operating cash generation: free cash flow of USD 107.4 million for nine months 2026 and USD 218.883 million for FY2025 on the company definition (Documentary Fact and Calculated figure from the financial base). (3) A diversified product and geographic base, with revenue in the Americas, EMEA and APAC and about 42% of FY2025 sales outside the U.S. (Documentary Fact). (4) A pre-deal balance sheet with trailing net leverage of 1.97x at FY2025 and interest cover on cash interest of 10.63x, showing capacity before the acquisition (Documentary Fact and Calculated figures). (5) Reporting transparency, including non-GAAP reconciliations and disclosure that purchase accounting is preliminary (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage of 5.57x total and 4.89x net on trailing Adjusted EBITDA that holds Ruckus for one quarter only (Calculated, Analyst Interpretation on its direction). (2) Unproven Ruckus earnings: a USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026 and goodwill and acquired intangibles of USD 2,040.8 million against stockholders' equity of USD 1,392.0 million (Documentary Fact). (3) Customer concentration through distributors and short-cycle orders (Documentary Fact). (4) Exposure to copper and tariff policy with only a lagged pass-through; earnings include tariff refunds (Documentary Fact; durability an Analyst Interpretation). (5) The term loan and revolver terms, ownership and ratings are not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, additional debt and collateral release cannot be judged (Insufficient Information).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Ruckus underdelivers | A USD 63.1 million pre-tax loss in Q3 2026 and preliminary accounting mean acquired earnings may fall short of the USD 1,850.0 million of new debt | Higher leverage for longer; debt service depends on legacy cash flow | Critical |

| Leverage tolerance undefined | The net leverage goal of about 1.5x was dropped from 2026 filings; no replacement is documented | Uncertain deleveraging path and possible resumption of buybacks ahead of debt reduction | Material |

| Distributor concentration | The ten largest customers are about 47% of FY2025 revenue, eight of them distributors, with no minimum purchases | Volume and working capital swing with channel behaviour | Material |
| Earnings quality | Adjusted EBITDA includes tariff refunds and adds back acquisition adjustments | Underlying margin may be lower than reported | Material |
| Documentation gap | Term Loan B, revolver and indenture terms are not supplied | Covenant headroom, guarantors and ranking cannot be assessed | Material |
| Euro exposure | The three euro notes total EUR 1,100.0 million; USD carrying values move with the euro | Translation changes reported debt | Minor |
## Calculations

No new calculation. Every figure above is copied from the financial base and business context handoffs: debt USD 1,291.950 million and USD 3,103.780 million; leverage 2.82x and 5.57x total, 1.97x and 4.89x net; liquidity USD 754.2 million; free cash flow USD 107.4 million and USD 218.883 million; cash interest cover 10.63x; net-expense cover 6.85x; goodwill and acquired intangibles USD 2,040.8 million. The Euro exposure row restates the EUR 1,100.0 million principal total from the financial base. Rounded figures in text (for example USD 59.4 million) restate the exact figures in those handoffs.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affects | Action |
| Term Loan B, revolver and indenture documents not supplied | High | Covenant headroom, ranking, guarantors, legal capacity | Obtain executed agreements |
| Ruckus pre-acquisition earnings and pro forma EBITDA not supplied | High | Combined leverage and interest cover Not calculable | Obtain pro forma EBITDA or run-rate |
| Cash interest paid for 2026 not supplied | Medium | Cash interest cover for Q3 2026 Not calculable | Use the FY2026 10-K supplemental disclosure |
| Ownership, beneficial holders and ratings not supplied | Medium | Control, activism and external credit view | Obtain the proxy statement and ratings |
| Segment history not comparable with 2026 | Low | Segment trend analysis | Use consolidated figures |

| Readiness: both upstream handoffs are limited rather than blocked; the readiness judgment of this module in the business context is ready with limitations | Medium | Confidence capped below High | Resolve the first four gaps |
## Next module

CP-5 should trace each figure in this module to the financial base and business context handoffs and check that the rounded figures match the exact ones. The open items for any later work are the term loan documents, the Ruckus earnings history and the cash interest paid.
